# convex_preview_deploy_key (Resource)

Manages a preview deploy key for a Convex project. Preview deploy keys let a CI or hosting integration spin up preview deployments, so they belong to a project rather than to any one deployment.

~> **The generated key is stored in Terraform state in plain text.** Convex returns the secret only once, at creation, so it cannot be read back. Treat the state file as a secret.

Convex offers no endpoint for changing a preview deploy key, so every attribute forces replacement.

Convex makes deploy key names unique by appending a suffix: a key created as `previews` is listed as `previews (<uuid>)`. The provider keeps `name` as configured and reports the full listed name in `unique_name`. Convex has no get-by-id endpoint, so reads list the project's keys and match on the stable `id`. A key with no `id` in state (an import, or state written by v0.2.0) is adopted by an exact match on `unique_name`, else by name. If that finds no single key, a key whose secret is in state is kept with a warning (destroy deletes it by the secret); otherwise a miss drops it from state and an ambiguous name fails, listing the candidates' ids. Names match when equal or when the listed one is the configured one plus a ` (<uuid>)` suffix.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "convex_project" "app" {
  team_id = var.convex_team_id
  name    = "My Application"
}

# Preview deploy keys belong to the project, not to a single deployment: they
# let CI or a hosting integration create preview deployments on demand.
resource "convex_preview_deploy_key" "vercel" {
  project_id = convex_project.app.id
  name       = "vercel"
}

# Feed the secret straight into whatever consumes it rather than printing it.
# This lands in Terraform state either way.
output "preview_deploy_key" {
  value     = convex_preview_deploy_key.vercel.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name the preview deploy key is created with. Convex appends a unique suffix when storing it, which is reported in `unique_name`; this attribute keeps the configured value. Changing this forces a new key.
- `project_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the project the key belongs to. Changing this forces a new key.

### Optional

- `expires_at` (Number) Timestamp in milliseconds at which the key expires. Must be at least 30 minutes in the future. Changing this forces a new key.

### Read-Only

- `allowed_actions` (Set of String) Actions the key is allowed to perform. Preview deploy keys are not configurable in this respect, so this reports whatever Convex granted.
- `creation_time` (Number) Creation timestamp, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
- `creator` (Number) Numeric member ID of whoever created the key.
- `id` (Number) Stable numeric identifier of the preview deploy key.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The generated preview deploy key. Available only on the apply that creates it; an imported key has this set to null.
- `last_used_time` (Number) Timestamp of the last use of this key, or null if it has never been used. Changes outside Terraform whenever the key is used.
- `unique_name` (String) The key's full name as Convex lists it, such as `previews (cbd71ace-cdac-417a-b967-78b318339e2e)`. Convex appends the suffix to make names unique; keys created before it did so have no suffix.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Preview deploy keys are imported as "<project_id>/<key_name>".
#
# As with regular deploy keys, <key_name> may be the name the key was created
# with or its full listed name, such as
# "vercel (cbd71ace-cdac-417a-b967-78b318339e2e)"; use the full name when
# several keys match the short one. Either way `name` is recorded as the short
# name and the full listed name as `unique_name`.
#
# The secret cannot be recovered, so the `key` attribute of an imported
# resource is null.
terraform import convex_preview_deploy_key.vercel 12345/vercel
# or, by the full listed name:
terraform import convex_preview_deploy_key.vercel '12345/vercel (cbd71ace-cdac-417a-b967-78b318339e2e)'
```
